newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian golfer Greg Norman has apparently not faced up to last year's loss of the 1996 US Masters Championship according to leading sports commentators. The resultant emotional baggage has been credited with causing Norman's hasty exit from this year's tournament where he missed the cut for only the third time in 17 years by adding a 74 to his first round 77 to finish on 151. Page 25.

Leading Australian Rugby Union player Richard Harry would like Australian selectors to consider the NSW state team front row as future national test team material. He claims that particular group of players can compete with the world's best. The Australan Waratah's destroyed world rugby's strongest provincial scrum on Saturday night when they defeated South Africa's Free State 36-11 at Sydney's Football Stadium. Page 27.

Defending national champions in Australia's basketball league competition, South East Melbourne Magic, have confirmed their favourite status for this year's title by defeating the Perth Wildcats by 104-84 in Perth on Friday night and following that up wit a 85-83 win against the Adelaide 36ers on Sunday. Page 27.

Australian international netball goal attack player Nicole Cusack will undergo an arthroscope to investigate her persistent knee injury that has kept her out of the opening round of the national netball competition. Cusack injured her knee during a pre-season tournament six weeks ago but was expected to recover in time for the start of the season. Page 27.
THE AGE

Australian marathon runner Steve Moneghetti has finished sixth in the London marathon yesterday. The loss was a disappointment as Moneghetti had been among the race leaders for most of the day and was ahead of the winner when the race had only three kilometres to go. The winner was Portugal's Antonio Pinot who set a record of two hours, seven minutes and 55 seconds. Page 2.

The Australian Football League (AFL) has again been pressured to initiate an expanded interchange bench. The renewed call came from coach Mick Malthouse of West Coast who yesterday criticised the AFL for the continuing injustice of the three-man system. As part of his call Malthouse urged for the scrapping of the reserve competition in order to facilitate a larger bench of players. Page 3.

Australian Michael Doohan yesterday launched his attempt for a fourth consecutive world championship in the world 500cc motorcycle title with a victory in the Malaysian Grand Prix at the Shah Alam course. The Australian won convincingly charging through to a early lead and winning by 11.796 seconds. Page 2. --

The South African cricket team scored a record 6/310 in its final one-day international match against Australia in Bloemfontein yesterday. Australia had already secured the series so South Africa was playing for pride. Australian bowlers could not prevail against the spirited South African batters with players such as Lance Klusener who made 92 runs off 115 balls, with seven fours and a six. Page 6.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian horse racing industry will review its field limits following the moveable rail at the Caulfied Cup being set out at the maximum 15 metres mark after a day of heavy racing yesterday. Acting chairman of stewards Terry Sharp said he would meet with other officials today to discuss the issue. Many jockeys have recently claimed the current field limits to be too restricting. Page 84.

Australian cycler Cadel Evans took a surprise win in round two of the mountain bike World Cup held in Wellington, New Zealand yesterday. Evans defeated more experienced European cyclers such as European champion Christophe Dupouey and world champion Jerom Chiotti. Evans now leads the series and is expected to win the championship. Page 86.

The Australian Football League is hauling another player, this time half-forward Nick Daffy from Richmond, before the AFL Tribunal on charges of foul play. The actions were captured on video and occurred on Saturday's match against the Western Bulldogs at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Daffy is one of several players to be caught out on video in the current competition round. Page 85.

The Australian Football League is considering allowing a live telecast of the Anzac Day match between Essendon and Collingwood in Melbourne. The major game is already heading for a sell-out as AFL chief executive officer Wayne Jackson indicated last nighthe would put the idea to Channel Seven today. Page 88.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Canberra Raiders appeared to have risen out of their slump yesterday with a 30-20 win against the Penrith Panthers at Penrith Stadium. Coach Mal Meninga hailed his players for a timely display of character. Page 37

Australian triathlete Matt Harris who competed in yesterday's Sport + Australian Ironman Triathlon has had his place in the competition disqualified. Harris who is well known among world Ironman circuits as an extrovert was disqualified for "mooning" the crowd during the competition's bike leg. He is the first competition in the sport's history to be disqualified for such a reason. Page 30.

The Australian racing industry is set for another clash with jockey's following a planned meeting by NSW owners today who are threatening to derail the start of the negotiations over jockey' fees. The NSW Racehorce Owners Association (NSWROA) is meeting o decide whether it will object to the appointment of Justice Reardon to handle the pay claims. Page 31.
